me7b7c4c96a05:
### Bit handling

#### Shift distance

Only the lowest {0} bits of the top int are used. A distance of {1} bits therefore acts as 0.

#### Vacated positions

{2}
mc280ded2681c:
### Integer division rules

#### Rounding

Truncate toward zero. For example, −7 ÷ 2 is −3.

#### Division by zero

A zero divisor throws ArithmeticException.

#### Minimum value ÷ −1

The result is the type’s minimum value. This overflow does not throw an exception.
m6c41c5afab95:
### Integer remainder rules

#### Sign

A nonzero result has the dividend’s sign. For example, −7 remainder 2 is −1.

#### Division by zero

A zero divisor throws ArithmeticException.

mb5fef8446838: The bytecode uses a signed 16-bit relative offset,from −32768 to 32767 bytes.
medf96a90b56a: The operand is a local slot index. Resumes within the same method at the returnAddress stored there; it does not pop an address from the stack.
mb8d8223c2f88: Pushes the next instruction's address as returnAddress,then jumps within the same method. The relative offset uses signed {0} bits.
m898b232a9448: Used by old finally implementations. Forbidden in class-file version 51.0 (Java 7) and later.
mc67f98dc5730: Allocates an instance of the named class. Fields start as 0,false or null,but the constructor has not run. Usually dup preserves the reference before invokespecial calls <init>. Abstract classes and interfaces cannot be instantiated.
m748964757650: Specify a primitive descriptor such as I (int) or Z (boolean),and push the length. Elements start as 0 or false. Zero length is valid; a negative length throws NegativeArraySizeException.
m3d3ceb7494b4: Specify a reference-type descriptor and push the length. Elements are null; their objects are not created. The element type may itself be an array. A negative length throws NegativeArraySizeException.
m13124e8fa297: Specify an array descriptor and how many dimensions to allocate. Push lengths from the outermost dimension inward. Deeper dimensions remain null if not allocated. The dimension count must be between 1 and the array type's rank. Lengths must be nonnegative; otherwise NegativeArraySizeException is thrown.
mecb86c0a4941: Returns the number of elements; the last index is length − 1. For multidimensional arrays,returns only the length of the referenced array. null throws NullPointerException.
m5ff568f2921a: Checks whether the reference can be treated as the specified class or interface. Success leaves the same reference; failure throws ClassCastException. null succeeds. This is not a numeric conversion.
mb7e36751d226: Pushes 1 if the referenced object is assignable to the specified type,otherwise 0. null produces 0. A mismatch does not throw ClassCastException.
m068607887077: Acquires the object's monitor,waiting if another thread owns it. Reentry by the owning thread increments its acquisition count. null throws NullPointerException.
mfa4caad4a1e0: Decrements the current thread's monitor count. At zero,other threads may acquire it. A non-owner gets IllegalMonitorStateException; null causes NullPointerException. Ensure every acquisition is released on both normal and exceptional exits.
ma198c4aad5d4: Does nothing and advances to the next instruction. Occupies one byte; it can reserve space for a patch.
mc0acbf21ca63: Widens the next load,store or ret local index to unsigned 16 bits. For iinc,also widens the increment to signed 16 bits. Does not change value types or precision. Together with the following opcode it forms one instruction; a branch cannot enter in the middle.
m759ef43d6cc4: Discards an unused value,such as a return value.
mbcc58ea38bc6: Removes one category-1 value. It cannot remove half of a long or double.
m45f907f7bf17: Removes two category-1 values or one long or double. A category-2 value cannot be split.
m8b3e25d0e365: Swaps TOP with the value below it. Both must be category 1; long and double cannot be swapped directly.
m11de3569c85d:
Keeps a copy before a calculation or store consumes the value. Copying a reference does not copy the object; both references point to the same object.

Rearrangement must not split a long or double. Check each form above for the required categories and value order.
m7b8bfb66b6a4:
Hello World opens on startup. Press Run at the top right. Its preset breakpoint pauses before invokevirtual; Debug shows the output stream and greeting on the stack. Press F8 to resume and print the greeting in Console.

Click between the line number and bytecode offset to remove the breakpoint. Without breakpoints, execution continues to the end.

The example folder contains arithmetic, branches, loops and arrays. Try changing the code. Reloading resets these examples; use File → Export JAL… to keep a copy.
m2181264bd49b:
Type an instruction to see completions. Fields and methods are also suggested after getstatic and invokestatic.

Hover an underline to read a diagnostic, or select it in Problems to jump to the source. Press Ctrl + . for available quick fixes.

Format with Shift + Alt + F. Labels align with the method declaration, one level outside instructions.

The numbers beside line numbers are bytecode offsets from the start of each method. They update without a build. Encoding changes during compilation can affect the final offsets.
me9b789cbc18a:
Instructions explains each instruction and includes examples. Click the search box to browse categories. Selecting an instruction closes the list. Clicking an instruction in the editor also opens its explanation.

Hover an instruction in an example to inspect the frame before and after it. TOP marks the top of the stack. Consumed values are red; added values are green. Locals appear when the instruction changes them.

Editor hovers use source analysis. Use Debug to inspect values while execution is paused.
mbb71c6101eac:
Click between a line number and its offset to set a breakpoint. Run pauses immediately before that instruction.

F8 resumes, F10 steps over, F11 enters a call, and Shift + F11 steps out. The floating controls provide the same actions. Stop ends execution.

Current shows the paused state; After shows the next instruction’s effect. Unknown results are represented by their type or an unknown value. Unchanged values appear in one column.

Select a caller frame to inspect its values at the call. The executing instruction is highlighted in the source. Native methods cannot be stepped into.
m2dc130c433c9:
Graph displays every method in the current class. Method outlines appear first; instructions and connections appear as analysis finishes.

Use the checkboxes to show stack, local-variable, control-flow and exception connections. Hide connections you do not need.

Click an instruction to jump to its source. Drag the background to pan; use the wheel to zoom.

Instructions are grouped into blocks. Exception connections lead from protected regions to handlers; exceptions sharing a route use one connection.
mab41ecfbaa24:
Press Shift twice to search files, classes and members. Enter part of a name and select a result.

Hold Ctrl and click a class or member, or press F12, to open its definition. OpenJDK classes are disassembled into JAL. Shift-click a label to visit its definition or uses.

Open a .class through File → Open… or drag it into the window. No project is required. Save the JAL with File → Export JAL….
maa27985d5312:
Choose File → Open folder… to work with multiple sources. Properties belong in .jalprj; sources remain separate files such as src/Main.jal. Folders without project properties also work. Opening a .jalprj asks you to select its source folder.

Choose the entry file in project properties. New projects default to src/Main.jal.

Save also preserves tab and window layouts; edits to example are excluded. Use ZIP export if the browser cannot write directly to a folder.

External changes are checked roughly once a second. If they conflict with unsaved edits, your edits are kept and a notice is shown.
m4caec0734b09:
Hold a tab briefly, then drag it to another group. Files in Project can also be dropped into a group.

Release a tab outside the window, or choose Open in separate window from its context menu, to detach it. Instructions, Graph and other panels can move too. Empty child windows close automatically.

Hover a tab to reveal its close button. Alt-click closes the other tabs in that group. Drag group boundaries to resize.

Choose View → Theme… to change colors and panel styling. The browser remembers your selection.
